title: Carnivals, road shows and soldiers' stories in Waco
summary: He recalls carnivals, minstrels and road shows, marching bands at the start of World War I, and soldiers' tales while he shined shoes.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years

blocks.x: Do you want to say anything about traveling shows?

Now what happened about the traveling shows, when I was about eight, in Waco, which we were still living in Waco, we used to have carnivals and they would have road shows and minstrels and things like that. But a kid seven years of age is not going to have an opportunity to learn... when I say to learn, I think to learn something about music, about dancing, you got to be exposed to it. You got to be up close to it. And we didn't have that opportunity. Later on we did, but this, you see, was about

the turn of the century; this was, when I say about the turn of the century, about 1914, when you had the war in Europe, and I used to sit around; then you started having marching bands--you know, drums and, you know, , and some blacks going into the army and some guy that probably could play the drums was a drummer, and then you had a trumpet player who could probably play that music of that age, you know, marching bands, you see. But then, shortly thereafter, I used to hear the men from Europe...you know, I used to sit around shining shoes in a shining parlor, and hear the soldiers that were being trained in America to be pilots and in other kinds of warfare and they used to just fascinate me with all these stories about London...London, you know!..but I didn't know where in the hell London was, you see. And then there were some strange things that we had there, that you wouldn't believe. You know, I used to believe when I was young that when it rained in Waco that it rained all over the world. I didn't have any idea that it rained in Waco and not rain in the next county. I thought that when it rained in Waco that was it, it was raining all over the world. These are unfortunate things, regrettably so, but then this is a fact.
